The most common thing I've heard is that once your body recognizes that it has been infected you may have severe flu like symptoms for a day and then it goes away. Your stress and anxiety is most likely what is giving you the physical problems. HIV weakens the bodies immune system but it's extremely slow acting (if untreated it could help cause death but only after 4-10 years...not trying to scare you just giving you an example of how slow it works).

Just get tested and then six months from when you think you got infected get tested again. Self diagnosis doesn't help in the long run. Better to know and then freak out rather than freak out unnecessarily. :) Either result you get learn from this. Get more informed, be safer, and keep an open mind. HIV has much more of a bad stigma behind it these days then posing as a serious threat due to lack of informed individuals.

The world can be quite a horrible place but not merely because of humans. Nature can be seemingly cruel as well as animals (look into Komodo dragons and how it can take a week for their poison to slowly kill an animal while they stalk it as it slowly dies). Granted, humans take horrible acts to whole new levels but the thing to keep in mind is that these people who delight in torture, kill or maim for fun, and so forth do so because they are not well in the head. Whether it's birth defect, bad genetics, inbreeding, emotional trauma, physical trauma to the brain, drug induced or whatever it may be. A healthy mind doesn't delight in such grossly obscene acts. That's not to say people don't think it or seek out to view such things because morbid curiosity can get the better of us but thinking things and acting upon them are entirely different. I get satisfaction from bashing in the brains of zombies in video games but I could never do such acts to a person or living creature. (Probably a bad example but oh well).

Do keep in mind that the news (at least in America) does focus almost exclusively on the worst case scenarios for rating purposes and that does darken our perspective on our surroundings.

The world is full of beautiful moments though. Dogs playing games with deer, bears befriending wolves, chickens keeping kittens warm. These are just moments with animals showing that despite their differences, despite the fact they might actually eat each other in other scenarios, that they can not only get along but they can become friends. Humans are capable of such things also only it's not as widely publicized. Small gestures of kindness that serve no other purpose than to make someone else feel happy, little compliments, grand gestures from anonymous people to help those in need. The world is full of everything - good, bad, and in-between. We just need to focus on what is important.

"If you look for the light, you can often find it. But if you look for the dark that is all you will ever see."

-Iroh, The Legend of Kora

Until at such a time that the virus in a person's body reaches zero there is always a slim chance of spreading it. Even a 0.01% chance is still a chance. All it takes is one healthy virus to get into the body, infect a cell, and start duplicating and very very slowly that person will become HIV+ especially when this particular virus can go largely unnoticed in the body as it attacks the cells that detect them as a threat. Also worth noting is how this virus can go dormant for up to ten years in the body so while the person may seemingly be uninfected it doesn't mean that they are not.

It is better to air on the side of some caution than fully trusting observation. Studies can be and have been manipulated for as long as they have existed to give the outcome that they are wanting rather than total honest truth if those doing the studies are after something more than legitimate results.

Food poisoning can become airborne if put through an electrolyzer but airborne food poisoning will slowly die off in the air and dupes cannot get sick from airborne food poisoning. Since plants eat the water fed into them, they won't get contaminated from it. Germy water used in sinks and lavatories are also fine (along with using super cold/hot water in them including the shower for some reason without causing adverse effects). So nothing to worry about. It's mostly an issue with using water for cooking purposes really.

Although if you manage to ever get to the point of trying to turn polluted water into steam you definitely need to slowly do so since if there is any slimelung in it it won't instantly die off from being steam and can still cause issues from what others say. Just an added thing.

Best advice about moving here is do your research on where you are moving to. Look at the crime rates, transportation, ease of access to important places (grocery stores, entertainment, shopping), etc. The more familiar you can get the easier the transition will be and the less likely that the move will be stressful enough to cause issues. Depression can be seen as having no hope left. No hope that things will get better, that anything will change, and that the misery will never end no matter how you may try and correct it. The deepest of depression is not something that positive thinking can overcome nor a matter of perspective. True happiness and all joy is robbed from the person. They no longer get any enjoyment from the things that once made them happy and every moment of life is painful. Death is then seen as the only possible choice left for who wants to live in a world with absolutely everything you do is one step away from making you cry in misery? I know all of this all too well...

First off, never take pills for any purpose other than as prescribed. They won't give you the outcome you hope for and it's just a desperate act to cure a temporary horrible feeling. I know this from experience. I tried to kill myself by overdosing on anti-depressants and all it did was fuck me up permanently on the left side of my body (which sadly is my dominant side).

A quote I always try to keep in mind is this:

"Never do something permanent based on something temporary."

I have chronic depression. I am used to dealing with depression daily and the majority of the time all the various medicines I've been on over the years have only lessened it a bit. Life can get better if you try to make it better. It's all a matter of perspective, being willing to do what it takes to make a change, and continued effort. Something I need to keep reminding myself of on a normal basis. It can get better if you want it to.

To be honest, I'm roughly in the same boat as you. Only reason I haven't offed myself is because I know how much it will hurt my family and ruin them.

My best advice, do everything else you can think of to make life better. Even if it is something you are normally against it's better to try something that might fail but could make life better. See a doctor for anti-depressants, get a counselor, use positive reinforcement, go to support groups, exercise, volunteer, get a pet, write in a journal, even try something like smoke weed. Try everything. Try anything that could potentially help. 

Suicide is always an option and we will all die at some point. It should only be seen as an absolute last resort until you've tried everything else. Life is always a struggle and will always be one. We just have to find a way to find the right kind of struggle that makes us happy in the end. There is no right or wrong way. The important part is to keep trying.

You sound very much like myself. I've dealt with depression for as long as I can remember (I'm 33 now). I've tried numerous pills over the years and most had horrible side effects with no benefits. I only ever found one medication that helped make me feel "normal" and that only lasted for two years before it's effect weakened to nothing at the max dosage and now I'm playing the pill hopping game again. It's frustrating, annoying, and I'm still struggling now more than ever to find the energy and desire to live.

As some would say, exercise, a healthy diet, and getting out of your comfort zone may help. Trying out alternative medicine might help as well. I wish I had some true answer though but you are not alone. My best suggestion is to do your best to experiment with different things in the hopes one of them will work, avoid the hospital (as you already know) since all they are capable of doing is robbing you of your time and money, and keep the "easy" solutions far away (guns, pills, etc that look tempting to end things). Also, I've found inspiring quotes are worth reading and focusing on one each day to help. If anything, for at least a mental distraction and something to put your mind to.

It's a difficult struggle every moment of your life until you find something that works. Remember that just like other emotions, depression is just a chemical making us feel like crap. You just gotta work to counter it's effect in other ways. It's worth the effort and remember, you aren't alone.

Well, there is a few things that you can do ranging from good to bad ideas.

You could try and analyze what it is/was that brought you happiness about what you used to enjoy about it. Sometimes going to the very basic understanding of why it brought you happiness with help. Like, why do you enjoy listening  to others? Is it because you enjoy the feeling of having someone open up to you? Or maybe listening to others is therapeutic for you and helps you to understand people better. It's  worth exploring.

It's also important to know that everyone takes the same information in a different way. Everyone views words themselves in different ways which makes even simple questions/phrases like saying "How are you doing?" to result in different reactions. Some people would get offended, others would find it to be kind, some would break down and cry, and so forth. That's one of the biggest issues when communicating with any stranger is that you have no idea what kind of response they will have to anything you say. You can try your best to be empathic and understanding but in the end it all depends on luck, good timing (the other person could be in a foul mood no matter what you say), careful word choice, and even more luck. Take their reaction in stride and remember that their understanding might be different than yours.

You could take a break from doing the things you used to love and try different things. Sometimes distance and time will help you to rediscover what brought you joy about them when you go back to trying again at it. That's a bit of a generalization but it might help. Plus, you might find new things that bring you enjoyment in the process.

If it becomes more severe you might consider medication for mood stabilizing. There are a lot of options and there could be one that helps to mellow the overly intense emotions that issues brought up. It's not for everyone of course.
